title: Mathematical analysis of a model for glycolytic oscillations in pancreatic $β$-cells
summary: Insulin secretion is pulsatile, with a period of about 5 min, coexisting with an ultradian rhythm (period of about 1 h), and a circadian (daily) rhythm. These rhythms are disrupted in type II diabetes. The 5-min rhythm is typically maintained even at fasting glucose levels, when there is no electrical activity in the insulin-secreting pancreatic $β$-cells.It has been proposed that this rhythm is due to oscillations in glycolysis, the first stage of glucose metabolism.
